(Background info is that I switched land to make my country look like it is on my personal map and this expansion with allow me to achieve that goal)

Part 1:
The Akhratian history is complex and unique, with each region being its own special land such as the mountains of Letent or the rolling hills of Glade or even the ancient forests of Rhaggue.

For over six centuries, the Empire of Akhratia has stood as one of the great civilizations of the world  a realm renowned not only for its stability and governance, but for the unmatched beauty of its culture. Guided by the enduring wisdom of the Imperial House of Vulpéčená, Akhratia has shaped a legacy that blends artistry, philosophy, and statesmanship into a civilization admired far beyond its frontiers.
Our history is not one of mere conquest, but of integration and cultivation. Under the Vulpéčená dynasty, provinces were not simply ruled  they were embraced. Local traditions were preserved, languages were nurtured, and Akhratian art, music, and architecture flourished into some of the most exquisite expressions of human creativity ever known. From the marble colonnades of Vulpécenas capital to the jeweled tapestries of the hill provinces, our culture became a shared treasure of the world.
The current division of our historic lands is an aberration of history  the result of outside intervention and opportunistic fragmentation during a brief moment of imperial weakness. These artificial borders have severed the natural economic, cultural, and familial bonds that for centuries united our heartlands with their peripheries.
Reunifying these territories under Akhratian stewardship is not expansion  it is restoration. It would mean the reestablishment of trade corridors that have carried goods and ideas for centuries, the safeguarding of cultural heritage sites that are the envy of nations, and the reweaving of a shared identity that has endured in the hearts of our people despite political separation.
The modern Akhratian state, guided by the traditions of the Vulpéčená family, remains uniquely suited to bring prosperity, security, and cultural vitality to these lands. Our right to govern is sanctified not only by six hundred years of history, but by the living will of those who still look to Akhratia as the rightful steward of their destiny.
Thus, the question before us is not whether Akhratia may expand its borders, but whether it will fulfill its sacred responsibility. For the sake of stability, unity, and the enduring splendor of the Akhratian civilization, the answer is the beauty of Akhratian civilization and culture 
 Part 2:

The Four Provinces  **Letent, Glade, Odepa, and Rhaggue**  have for centuries formed the cultural, spiritual, and economic foundation of the Akhratian Empire. Bound together under the guidance of the Imperial House of Vulpéčená, they are more than territories: they are the living memory of our civilization and the holiest lands of the Celestine faith.

**Letent**  Guarding the Empires northern frontier, Letent is a province of soaring peaks, glacial rivers, and mountain monasteries. Its high valleys cradle the **Sanctuary of the First Light**, the most sacred site in all of Celestine  believed to be where the heavens first touched the earth and bestowed divine blessing upon the Akhratian people. Pilgrims travel across continents to walk the sanctuarys ancient stone steps, seeking the same light that shone upon the first prophets.

**Glade**  To the west, Glade stretches in golden plains and fertile farmlands, famed for sustaining the Empires earliest generations. It was in Glade that the first imperial charter was signed, uniting Akhratias tribes beneath the Vulpéčená crown. The province is home to the **Hall of Concord**, where Celestine tradition holds that the founding rulers received divine guidance in forging the realm. Even today, Glade is seen as the Empires granary and a symbol of unity blessed by heaven.

**Odepa**  The eastern province of Odepa is a land of forests, rivers, and scholarly cities, long regarded as the Empires center of learning. Its great libraries hold illuminated manuscripts of the Celestine canon alongside the philosophical works of countless cultures. Odepas **Monastery of the Sapphire Veil** is revered in Celestine tradition as the place where the Prophet Arien meditated for forty days, emerging with visions that shaped the faiths sacred calendar.

**Rhaggue**  To the south lies Rhaggue, the only coastal province of Akhratia, where verdant hills roll down to the azure sea. For Celestines, Rhaggue is the site of the **Garden of the Four Winds**, a place where the sea breezes are believed to carry prayers directly to the divine. The coastal city of Velthar serves as the chief port for pilgrims arriving from distant lands, making Rhaggue not just a holy place but the Empires gateway to the world.

---

**The Sacred Unity of the Provinces**
Though diverse in landscape and custom, the Four Provinces are united by the Celestine faith, which recognizes them collectively as the Blessed Quadrant  the lands most favored by the divine. For six centuries, they have been the heart of Akhratias identity, bound together by faith, trade, and the enduring rule of the Vulpéčená dynasty.

To separate these provinces from Akhratia is to disrupt not only political unity but the spiritual harmony of our civilization. To restore them is to heal the body of the Empire and safeguard the holiest lands of Celestine for generations to come.

[u][b]Embassy Hostage Crisis[/b][/u]
The younger ISRP officer jogged to the rear of a tactical vehicle, retrieving a military-grade loudspeaker. Without hesitation, he walked to the center of the street, exposed, calm, and raised the device.

[b]ISRP Translator[/b]
 WE KNOW YOU ARE IN THERE! WHAT ARE YOUR DEMANDS?

The voice echoed down the block, bouncing between buildings, as dozens of lenses from rooftop scopes adjusted and waited.
A long minute passed.

Thenmovement.

A woman stumbled out of the embassys front doors, barefoot, shaken, her arms raised. Her right hand clutched a folded piece of paper. The ISRP translator, hand extended, motioned her forward.
Slowly, she crossed the space, eyes flicking from sniper nests to armored turrets, until she reached the police perimeter. KGI officers rushed to secure and escort her. Paramedics arrived in seconds, whisking her toward the trauma ambulance under full escort.

The translator stepped back, unfolded the note, and passed it to the KGI Commander.

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 We demand the immediate release of all land illegally held by Roskesak and 

(his voice trailed off, the rest he muttered under his breath before stopping)

 Theyre asking for something completely unreasonable. We couldnt give it even if we wanted to.

From behind, the older ISRP operative keyed into his earpiece, listening intently. After a brief pause, he murmured something in Llyndorran to the translator.

[b]ISRP Translator[/b]
 Are your men ready to breach?

The KGI Commander raised his radio.

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 Teams Alpha and Bravo, status?

A beat passed...

[b]Alpha Lead (Radio)[/b]
 Standing by. Charges set.

[b]Bravo Lead (Radio)[/b]
 On mark. Visuals are clear.

(The Commander nodded)

 [b]KGI Commander[/b]
 Yes. Were ready.

The translator turned back and gave a quiet nod to his partner. Without ceremony, the older ISRP officer spoke a single coded phrase into his wrist mic. Unbeknownst to the Commander, ISRP intelligence teams had already confirmed the position of every assailant inside. One had remained dangerously close to the hostages in the consular wing, but the rest were spread too thin. Isolated. Vulnerable.
And one just made a fatal mistake.

Curtains twitched on a second-floor window.

A shoulder moved into frame.

That was all it took. An earsplitting crack rang out like a thunderclap. From the rooftop of Building 3A, a 13.2mm armor-piercing round vaporized the upper window and dropped the suspect in a single hit, one shot, one kill.

Immediately, all comms went hot.

[b]ISRP (Radio)[/b]
 Alpha confirmed. Execute breach.

With military precision, KGI and ISRP operators stormed the embassy. A dual stack breached the side entrance with a deafening bang. Flashbangs burst through the lobby. Another unit rappelled to the roof, cutting through skylights with thermal torches.

(Inside, terrorists panicked)

Rooms were cleared in rapid succession and tight, silent formations; rooms were marked in chalk as secure. One suspect fled down a stairwell and was tackled at the landing by a KGI assault team. Another dropped his weapon and surrendered in the cafeteria. A third opened fire from the archive hall and was neutralized instantly by two ISRP operators.
Three minutes in the entire embassy were cleared. Over comms, the all-clear tone sounded.

[b]ISRP Officer (Radio)[/b]
 Objective secure. Suspects neutralized or in custody. Zero civilian casualties.

The KGI Commander entered the embassys foyer, rifle lowered, boots crunching on broken glass. The flag of Roskesak still stood above the central desk, bullet holes in the marble, but standing proud.
He exhaled once. It was over.
